newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-NO AGREEMENT YET IN ARGENTINE STRIKE TALKS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NO AGREEMENT YET IN ARGENTINE STRIKE TALKS.

text.p: Argentina's professional soccer players began what was likely to be a very short-lived strike on Wednesday to call for six Deportivo Espanol players to be free to transfer to other clubs.

But Argentine Football Association (AFA) officials said they trusted the government would order both sides to begin a period of compulsory negotiations to end the dispute and meanwhile tell players to get back on the pitches.
AFA and players' representatives met for 2-1/2 hours for a conciliation meeting at the Labour Ministry on Wednesday but failed to reach an agreement and adjourned talks until Thursday.
"Until tomorrow there will be no more news. We've been summoned for 12 noon (1500 GMT)," footballers' union leader Sergio Marchi said.
Players said they will continue to train but will not take part in any league matches, next scheduled for Sunday.
"This strike is to demand respect for the players of Deportivo Espanol," River Plate full-back Eduardo Berizzo told reporters after the vote on Tuesday night.
However, a Libertadores Cup match on Wednesday between Racing Club and Sporting Cristal of Peru will go ahead because it is organised by the South American Football Federation and not AFA.
The strike comes after six players decided to leave troubled first-division side Deportivo Espanol when their contracts expired on June 30.
But a judge ruled that the players count as assets of the heavily-indebted club, and so cannot leave until all creditors have been paid.
"This is black or white. There is no possibility of negotiation," said Fernando Quiroz, who was due to face Sporting Cristal for Racing Club at 9 p.m. (midnight GMT).
